China Focus: AI breathes new life into China's time-honored TCM tradition
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
14:20:36 CST
15:20:36 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Type in a question about how different herbal medicines should be combined, and within seconds, a smartphone can display the logic behind the formula, along with the principles underpinning it.
For students studying traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), this AI tool is becoming a new kind of "digital teaching assistant," offering help beyond the classroom.
Led by Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, developers have built a large model incorporating vast TCM knowledge, including classical texts and theories, teaching materials, herbal medicines and prescriptions.
Another notable example is an embodied intelligent robot developed by this university, which is able to demonstrate traditional TCM massage techniques.
For centuries, TCM knowledge has been passed down through classical texts, apprenticeships with experienced physicians and hands-on clinical practice.
Preserving and transmitting this accumulated knowledge has long been a challenge for TCM education. Now, AI is making its way into China's higher TCM education system, opening up new methods to pass on this time-honored medical tradition.
Li Ziyuan, a doctoral student at Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine, located in south China, said AI can organize ancient medical texts, analyze the clinical experience of senior TCM practitioners and assist with medication recommendations, thus shortening the learning curve for young physicians.
Huang Luqi, a TCM expert, noted that AI can systematically capture the diagnostic approaches, distinctive techniques and time-tested prescriptions of renowned practitioners from the grassroots level.
This can turn fragmented, experience-based knowledge into standardized and shareable data, helping preserve valuable local TCM expertise and pass it on to future generations, Huang, also an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, added.
China inaugurated its modern higher TCM education system in 1956. Seven decades later, the country has 27 independently established undergraduate institutions specializing in TCM, while about 670 higher education institutions offer TCM-related programs. More than 800,000 students are enrolled.
As of the end of 2025, the total number of health professionals in TCM-related healthcare institutions had reached 1.236 million, up nearly 49 percent from 2020. Also in 2025, TCM medical visits made up 20.3 percent of all medical visits nationwide.
TCM diagnosis traditionally relies on four methods: observation, listening and smelling, inquiry, and pulse-taking. Practitioners combine the information gathered through these methods to assess a patient's condition and determine treatment.
AI is now being used to explore ways of digitizing these traditional diagnostic techniques.
At a TCM hospital in Zhuhai, south China's Guangdong Province, a "smart clinic" can automatically collect patients' tongue, facial and pulse information. It uses a large model to assist physicians with clinical decision-making and provide intelligent follow-up services.
AI-assisted diagnosis could make TCM diagnostic information more objective and quantifiable, reducing subjectivity in manual assessment, Huang said, noting that it could also provide references for treatment plans and help improve the precision of TCM services at the grassroots level.
China is also making AI a part of its national strategy for advancing TCM. A 2026-2030 blueprint calls for greater use of digital and intelligent technologies in TCM and the development of high-quality datasets in this field.
As AI becomes more deeply embedded in TCM education and practice, questions about the limits of the technology are becoming increasingly important.
Zhao Leyi, a student at Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, said AI can make the tacit knowledge accumulated by veteran practitioners more accessible for learning and transmission, but cannot replace the core reasoning involved in TCM.
Final decisions on diagnosis and treatment must be grounded in TCM theories, therapeutic principles and the system of traditional medicinal practice, Zhao explained.
The intuitive and experience-based understanding of life phenomena accumulated by physicians over centuries deserves more systematic study, so that the wisdom of ancient medicine can be explored from new scientific perspectives, said Ji Guang, president of Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine. ■

Young people's violence without ideology poses emerging extremism threat: study
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
14:20:14 CST
15:20:14 KST

SYDNEY, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Young people committing or threatening violence without a clear ideological, religious or political motive are posing an emerging extremism threat, researchers in Australia have warned.
A review led by University of Queensland (UQ) criminologist Professor Adrian Cherney examined the rise of what is known as Nihilistic Violent Extremism (NVE), and the significant challenges it poses for traditional interventions, according to a UQ statement released on Monday.
"Acts of violent extremism have historically been underpinned by ideological radicalization, but we're now seeing cases in which the violence itself appears to be the primary attraction," said Cherney, lead author of the review published in the Journal for Deradicalization.
Unlike traditional violent extremism driven by political or religious goals, NVE can focus on spectacle, notoriety and creating chaos and collapse, fueled by harmful online communities and subcultures that normalize and celebrate violence, he said, adding that NVE can be a way to "gain validation, status or acceptance in those groups."
Social isolation, a search for identity and belonging, along with emotional drivers such as loneliness, hostility and contempt, can make vulnerable young people susceptible, while many cases involve trauma, abuse, bullying or family dysfunction, Cherney said.
The review found NVE poses challenges for existing tools and models used to counter extremism and identify people at risk, as those frameworks can require evidence of extremist ideology before intervention.
The researchers recommended considering behavioral warning signs, online signaling and a fascination with violence alongside traditional indicators of radicalization, and called for greater integration among youth justice, child protection, education and law enforcement to assess risks and provide appropriate interventions. ■

bomb cloud sculpture takes shape in soil, straw and water inside abandoned lisbon school
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
06:15:00 UTC
15:15:00 KST

earth, straw, sand, water, and wood form The Weight of the Soil
The Weight of the Soil is a large-scale sculpturalinstallation by Iranian-born, Brooklyn-based artists Saman & Sasan Oskouei, installed inside an abandoned school in Lisbon. The work gives physical form to the fleeting image of a bomb cloud, using adobe, soil, straw, sand, water, and wood to slow down a moment of destruction and give it material weight.
Constructed in situ, the sculpture uses a minimal wood structure covered with layers of adobe made from soil, sand, straw, and water. The earthen material was built up by hand into irregular, cloud-like masses, leaving the texture and character of the soil visible across the surface. Rather than depicting the explosion itself, the installation focuses on what follows: dust settling, material hardening, and the transformation of destruction into landscape.
the installation is constructed in situ inside abandoned school
The use of earth introduces a central contrast within the work by artists Saman & Sasan Oskouei. A material traditionally associated with shelter, home, and permanence is shaped into an image of destruction. The installation’s earthen construction also connects the bomb cloud to the physical ground, turning an image usually encountered for only a few seconds through photographs, videos, and screens into a lasting spatial presence.
The work occupies an abandoned school that had been unused for approximately 15 years. Its worn architecture, tiled walls, damaged ceiling, and traces of former use become part of the installation. A building associated with learning and the future provides the setting for a form associated with destruction and its aftermath.
As the dust settles and the adobe hardens, the bomb cloud becomes a landscape. The work considers how violence extends beyond the moment of impact, becoming embedded in memory, architecture, landscapes, and the ground itself.

====================================================================================================

Indonesia Finally Has Its Aircraft Carrier. Now Comes the Hard Part.
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
06:05:00 UTC
15:05:00 KST

Last year, reports surfaced that Indonesia was considering acquiring an aircraft carrier for the first time in its history. This prompted a heated debate over whether Indonesia truly needed an aircraft carrier. In an article published in The Diplomat, I argued that Indonesia didn’t need such an acquisition, at least for the time being, for a variety of reasons. The arrival of the KRI Sriwijaya, as the new vessel is known, thus marks the end of one discussion and the start of another. The key question now is whether Indonesia can turn the ship into a sustainable military capability.
On September 18, the aircraft carrier, formerly known as ITS Giuseppe Garibaldi, arrived at Tanjung Priok Port in Jakarta. The ship was personally welcomed to port by the minister of defense, the commander of the Indonesian National Armed Forces, and the chief of naval staff. A formal handover from the Italian Navy to the Indonesian Navy took place on September 24, at which the carrier was reflagged and christened with its new name,
The name chosen by the Indonesian government has important symbolic importance. Sriwijaya was a strong monarchy and a respected naval power in Sumatra from the 7th to the 13th centuries.
However, with the ship’s arrival, the most important question is whether and how Indonesia can convert the ship into a viable military asset?
A Ship Doesn’t Equal Capabilities
Aircraft carriers are often associated with naval superiority. Their ability to carry and operate aircraft or helicopters from the sea provides flexibility in projecting power, extending a navy’s range of operations, while also offering strategic options that do not entirely depend on land-based airfields. Moreover, the possession of an aircraft carrier with its various strategic values also brings prestige.
However, an aircraft carrier is not an arms technology that can produce strategic effects independently. Like other conventional weapon technologies, the effectiveness of an aircraft carrier heavily relies on the supporting ecosystem that enables it to operate sustainably and safely. In general, aircraft carriers never sail independently. In operation, the aircraft carrier will be part of a carrier strike group (CSG), which usually consists of an aircraft carrier, a guided missile cruiser, anti-aircraft warships, and anti-submarine destroyers or frigates. In carrying out its operations, the aircraft carrier is also often escorted by attack submarines.
The ITS Giuseppe Garibaldi was always escorted by other warships while still flying the Italian flag. For example, during the Passing Exercise in the Mediterranean Sea in 2020, Garibaldi was accompanied by at least two multirole frigates and one supply ship.
In a CSG, each element has a complementary function, ranging from air defense, anti-submarine warfare, protection of the aircraft carrier, logistics, to command and control. Therefore, the capabilities produced by the CSG are the result of the integration of various platforms, not merely a consequence of the presence of an aircraft carrier itself.
In the context of Indonesia, the issue of the availability of escort and support fleets for aircraft carrier operations becomes is a very important issue. Indonesia indeed now has its long-awaited carrier, but still lacks surface warships to form a CSG as commonly found in the United States or French navies. Referring to the Laboratorium Indonesia 2045 database, Indonesia still lacks 12 frigates and seven fast missile boats to fulfil the government’s Archipelagic Trident Shield defense posture goals. The same goes for the submarine fleet. Indonesia is recorded to still be short of at least eight submarines.
A Carrier For Disaster Operations
The government and the Indonesian National Armed Forces (TNI) have indeed stated on several occasions that the presence of KRI Sriwijaya is not intended for expeditionary combat missions. They argue that the aircraft carrier will instead be prioritized for military operations other than war, specifically humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR). For instance, once operational, the government stated that KRI Sriwijaya would join other TNI forces to assist in handling the ongoing forest fires in Kalimantan. In addition to HADR missions, the Indonesian Navy chief of staff has said that the carrier will be used for defense diplomacy activities, such as port visits.
At first glance, the government’s and TNI’s statement to prioritize HADR missions and defense diplomacy for KRI Sriwijaya sounds rational. Besides the fact that Indonesia’s military posture does not allow for offensive operations, this statement is also expected to prevent diplomatic tensions with other countries, especially in the region.
However, this again raises the question of whether Indonesia truly requires an aircraft carrier. HADR can be a relevant mission for KRI Sriwijaya, but the relevance of a mission does not automatically prove that the chosen platform is the most effective way to achieve that capability. To ensure that KRI Sriwijaya can fulfill its role, Indonesia must still build the right ecosystem around it. For example, if it is intended for HADR missions on land, then Indonesia must ensure the availability of adequate transport helicopters. If Indonesia does not invest in acquiring a sufficient number of transport helicopters, then the KRI Sriwijaya will only become a sitting duck in the middle of the Nusantara sea when a disaster occurs on land.
In other words, if Sriwijaya is to be used for HADR missions, the measure of its success should not stop at the ship’s ability to carry helicopters to disaster areas. A more important question is whether the entire ecosystem built around the ship produces HADR capabilities that are significantly higher than the simpler and more cost-effective alternatives. At this point, Indonesia needs to realistically define the capabilities that it actually wants to derive from Sriwijaya so that it can then build the appropriate ecosystem around it.

China Conducts Military Exercise in South China Sea After Confrontation at Disputed Shoal
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
05:35:00 UTC
14:35:00 KST

China’s military conducted a joint training exercise around the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea, it announced yesterday, two days after the Philippines accused Beijing of obstructing a resupply mission in another part of the contested waterway.
The People’s Liberation Army Southern Theater Command said in a statement on WeChat that the combined air and naval drill was a necessary response to actions by “certain countries” that it said had undermined regional peace and stability, Reuters reported.
The exercise “aims to test and enhance combat capabilities in safeguarding China’s territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests,” the Southern Theater Command said.
The China Coast Guard announced separately that the exercises focused on “maritime rights-protection, law enforcement, and management and control” in the waters around Scarborough Shoal.
A triangular atoll that sits around 200 kilometers to the west of the Philippines’ Luzon Island and 874 kilometers from China’s Hainan Island, Scarborough Shoal has been a persistent flashpoint in the maritime disputes between the Philippines and China. The shoal has been under Chinese control since 2012, when the two nations engaged in a tense 10-week stand-off that concluded with China occupying the feature, despite an agreement for mutual withdrawal from the shoal.
Since then, China Coast Guard (CCG) vessels have surrounded the shoal and made repeated attempts to restrict Filipino fishermen from accessing the rich fishing grounds inside the atoll’s central lagoon.
While the Chinese military did not specify which “certain countries” were the pretext for the joint exercises, it is not hard to guess.
Two days earlier, Manila accused the CCG of obstructing a resupply mission to troops stationed at Second Thomas Shoal in the Spratly Islands, prompting a strong rebuke from the Chinese government.
In a statement on Friday, Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson Jay Tarriela said that the mission, which aimed to resupply the troops stationed aboard the BRP Sierra Madre, the grounded warship that functions as Manila’s foothold on the shoal, was “temporarily suspended after a CCG vessel carried out dangerous maneuvers” against the Philippine resupply vessel M/V Lapu-Lapu. The maneuvers “put Filipino personnel at risk” and prevented the mission from being completed, he said.
“There was no collision, and no one was injured, but the dangerous maneuvers of the China Coast Guard created a serious risk of collision,” Tarriela added.
For its own part, CCG spokesperson Jiang Lue accused the PCG of engaging in “provocative” acts at Second Thomas Shoal, restating its position that the BRP Sierra Madre was illegally grounded on the shoal in 1999.
“China Coast Guard, in accordance with the law, took measures including on-site monitoring and following, as well as issuing verbal warnings to the Philippine resupply vessel,” it stated. It added that the CCG “will resolutely safeguard China’s territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests.”
In a statement, the U.S. embassy in Manila condemned the Chinese action and lauded its Philippine allies’ “professionalism and restraint.”
“The United States strongly condemns the use of dangerous blocking and other irresponsible maneuvers by the China Coast Guard and the People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) that threatened a collision with a Philippine vessel and prevented a lawful and routine resupply mission to Second Thomas Shoal,” it said.
In what has now become a predictable pattern, the Chinese embassy responded by condemning the U.S. for its “insistence on supporting the Philippines’ provocative and unlawful actions at Ren’ai Reef.”
“China urges the U.S. side to stop fanning the flames and refrain from actions that undermine regional peace and stability,” it said.
Friday’s incident comes just over two months after a serious confrontation at Second Thomas Shoal, in which a Philippine Navy marine sustained a head injury after being struck with a baton by CCG personnel, who were taking photos and videos of the grounded warship.
This broke a period of relative calm at Second Thomas Shoal, following a string of increasingly dangerous confrontations between the two sides in 2023 and 2024. These incidents, which stemmed mostly from Chinese attempts to prevent the resupply of the Philippine forces aboard the BRP Sierra Madre, culminated in a July 2024 melee between the CCG and PCG that left eight Philippine naval personnel injured, including one who lost a thumb in the fighting. The two sides subsequently agreed to de-escalate the situation at Second Thomas Shoal, reaching a “provisional understanding” that allowed the Philippines to resupply the grounded warship.
Friday’s interdiction attempt suggests that this “provisional understanding” between Manila and Beijing has now broken down, potentially ushering in a new period of tension at Second Thomas Shoal.

Citizen-Led Campaign Seeks UNESCO Status for Select Pre-Colonial Sites in Lima, Peru
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
05:30:00 UTC
14:30:00 KST

A campaign led by Red Lima Milenaria is seeking UNESCO recognition for pre-colonial sites in the Peruvian capital. Today, more than 600 archaeological sites remain in Lima, a metropolis of 11 million people. The citizens' campaign seeks to improve conservation conditions and public awareness of the sites that resisted European colonization by promoting the nomination of a selection of structures for inscription on UNESCO's World Heritage List. The public campaign was recently launched to gather citizen support and establish partnerships with organizations working in heritage and related fields, in order to prepare the framework for a formal nomination to be submitted by the Peruvian state. The initiative coincides with reconstruction movements in the continent responding to socioeconomic inequality and structural historical injustices, raising questions about the very definition of heritage.
Sites awaiting preservation are known as huacas (or wak'a), commonly understood as sacred places believed to hold spiritual power and a connection to ancestors or deities in traditional Andean culture. According to César Itier, "huaca" actually meant "split," referring to portable stones considered fragments or duplicates of a mythical ancestor residing on a hill. The term was therefore applied to the sanctuary that housed these stones, to the divine ancestor himself, and to the stone amulets that emanated from him. The remaining sites are today embedded among the homes, roads, and high-rise buildings of contemporary Lima, many of them facing intense urban pressure and inadequate maintenance. Today, ahead of Peru's forthcoming municipal elections, the campaign seeks to place their future within the debate over how Lima develops.
 UNESCO recognition would bring greater international visibility to this extraordinary heritage. For the people of Lima, however, the real challenge is to recognise the huacas as an essential part of our identity and integrate them into the life of the city. ― Javier Lizarzaburu, founder of Red Lima Milenaria
The campaign also aims to raise awareness about past ways of life and build contemporary appreciation for those cultural traditions. As Red Lima Milenaria states, "for almost five centuries, the capital's dominant historical narrative has largely treated the colonial period as its starting point." The list of sites is composed of places that bear witness to the diversity of societies that once inhabited Peruvian territory, including monumental structures built of earthen materials and ancient irrigation systems still in operation. A preliminary survey accompanying the campaign places Lima among the few capital cities in the world, along with Amman, Yerevan, Jerusalem, Cairo, Abu Dhabi, Manama, and Beirut, that retain architecture dating back approximately 4,000 years or more within their urban or metropolitan areas. The campaign's outreach efforts are therefore also aimed at promoting its international significance.
The group of potentially nominated sites includes El Paraíso huaca in the district of San Martín de Porres (2000 B.C.); the Pucllana huaca in Miraflores (5th century A.D.); the Campoy fortress in San Juan de Lurigancho (12th century A.D.); and sections of the Surco Canal in San Borja, among others. Two thousand years ago, other notable civilizations flourished beyond the Maya and the Incas, such as the Han Dynasty in China and the Roman Empire in the Mediterranean basin. For these Andean archaeological sites to receive similar recognition from UNESCO, the application needs to demonstrate that the cultural sites are historically authentic in materials, design, and setting; meet at least one of ten official selection criteria; and show that they can have adequate local legal protection, among other requirements of the multi-step nomination and evaluation process.
Other recent news from Latin America includes Frida Escobedo Studio's new project for the renovation of the Museum of Latin American Art (MALBA) in Buenos Aires, an underground extension celebrating the cultural institution's 25th anniversary. Also in Buenos Aires, the Argentine International Architecture Biennial celebrates 40 years of history this year, with an edition featuring representatives from more than 55 cities worldwide, in a free, open program running for five weeks. In Chile, local heritage is also being claimed as a subject of value and study, with a learning and collaboration event centered on Valparaíso's traditional construction trades, "Oficios en obra," running from October 9 to 11.

BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China's industrial profits maintained double-digit growth in the first eight months of 2026, driven by the rapid expansion of high-tech manufacturing and new growth drivers, official figures showed Monday.
Profits of industrial firms above designated size increased 15.7 percent year on year during the first eight months of 2026, according to National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) data.
These industrial firms with an annual main business revenue of at least 20 million yuan (about 2.97 million U.S. dollars) saw their combined profits reach 5.27 trillion yuan in the January-August period.
In the three major sectors, mining industry profits jumped 35.1 percent to 766.15 billion yuan, and manufacturing profits climbed 17.4 percent to nearly 3.97 trillion yuan. Profits in the power, heat, gas and water production and supply sector fell 12 percent to 536.3 billion yuan.
Yu Weining, an NBS statistician, attributed the relatively fast profit growth to the steady advance of industrial production and the widened increase in industrial product prices.
Yu highlighted the electronic sector as the main pillar, with profits surging 110 percent year on year, contributing 62 percent to the overall profit growth of industrial firms.
"The accelerated expansion of new technology applications represented by artificial intelligence has driven the expansion of demand in related fields, propelling rapid profit growth in the electronics industry," Yu said.
Yu noted that rising chip demand driven by emerging scenarios such as new energy vehicles, the Internet of Things and computing power centers boosted profits in the optoelectronic device manufacturing and semiconductor discrete device manufacturing industries by 72 percent and 51.8 percent, respectively.
High-tech manufacturing played a prominent role in driving growth. During the January-August period, profits of high-tech manufacturing firms above designated size rose 54.7 percent year on year, 39 percentage points higher than the overall growth rate.
In August alone, profits of major industrial firms grew 4.2 percent year on year, according to the NBS. ■

Eighth round of China-U.S. economic and trade consultations yields positive consensus: commerce ministry
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
13:29:41 CST
14:29:41 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China and the United States held the eighth round of their economic and trade consultations in New York and Washington, D.C., the United States, from Sept. 20 to 23, reaching positive consensus that contributes to the economic and trade outcomes of the meeting of the two heads of state, China's Ministry of Commerce said on Monday.
The two sides agreed to establish the Board of Trade under the China-U.S. economic and trade consultation mechanism, with the primary target of optimizing bilateral trade, the ministry noted in a statement.
The ministry said the Board of Trade will provide an important platform and institutional guarantee for the two countries to continuously expand the list of cooperation and shorten the list of problems in economic and trade affairs.
To implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, China and the United States have held multiple rounds of consultations under the Board of Trade framework on an arrangement for a 30-billion-U.S. dollar reciprocal tariff reduction, and have reached consensus, the ministry said.
The two sides agreed to reduce tariffs on about 30 billion U.S. dollars' worth of goods imported from each other on a reciprocal basis, with tariffs on around 90 percent of the covered products to be lowered to most-favored-nation rates. These reductions will be implemented simultaneously after each side completes domestic legal procedures, according to the ministry.
The economic and trade teams of the two sides agreed to include Chinese coal imports from the United States in the reciprocal tariff reduction framework, which is expected to facilitate Chinese coal imports from the United States in 2027 and 2028, the ministry revealed.
Importing U.S. coal will complement China's domestic coal market while providing stable revenue and employment for the U.S. coal industry, helping to stabilize and expand bilateral trade, the ministry explained.
In the consultations, China and the United States also agreed to establish the Board of Investment under the China-U.S. economic and trade consultation mechanism. It will provide an institutionalized communication platform for both sides, with the two countries' economic and trade teams conducting regular dialogue on potential investment opportunities and barriers, the ministry said.
The two sides further agreed to establish an agricultural working group under the Board of Trade, to be co-chaired by China's Ministry of Commerce and the Office of the United States Trade Representative, with participation from relevant regulatory agencies of both countries, said the ministry.
The working group will discuss issues including two-way market access and regulatory matters for agricultural products. Both sides agreed to hold the working group's first meeting before the end of 2026, the ministry said.
The two sides reached a consensus in principle on financial services. China will examine and approve applications from financial service institutions of all countries, including those with U.S. capital, to conduct business and establish branches in China.
China hopes the United States will also provide a fair, transparent and stable policy environment for Chinese financial institutions, said the ministry.
As the two sides' lead negotiators under the China-U.S. economic and trade consultation mechanism, Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent established a dialogue on artificial intelligence (AI) and held their first discussion on AI-related risks and benefits. The two sides agreed to hold the next dialogue before the end of November this year and to set up a communication channel for AI incidents.
On the basis of extending the joint arrangements of economic and trade consultations in Kuala Lumpur through Jan. 10, 2027, China and the United States agreed to continue actively discussing the issue, with a view to reaching a mutually agreed solution.
Such an arrangement, on the one hand, gives both sides room to take stock of and assess the implementation of the joint arrangements and consider how to move China-U.S. economic and trade relations forward. On the other hand, by combining a time-bound extension with continued active discussions, it provides a relatively stable and predictable policy environment for cooperation between businesses of the two countries, according to the ministry.
It is believed that the two sides will continue their efforts and seek a positive solution on a further extension through high-level economic and trade interactions before the end of the year, the ministry noted.
The two sides also exchanged views on increasing direct passenger flights between the two countries, agreeing to maintain communication on increasing China-U.S. flights and related matters.
Since last year, China and the United States have held eight rounds of economic and trade consultations. During the latest consultations, the two sides reaffirmed and renewed their commitment to fully implementing the consensus reached in previous rounds of economic and trade talks, which will help create favorable conditions and a stable environment for bilateral economic and trade cooperation, while also contributing to global economic growth, said the ministry. ■

Watch: Landslide blocks Kedarnath route in Rudraprayag’s Chirbasa, over 1,500 pilgrims evacuated
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
05:24:55 UTC
14:24:55 KST

Kedarnath route blocked by landslide in Rudraprayag's Chirbasa village
NEW DELHI: Around 1,500 pilgrims stranded on the Kedarnath route near Chirbasa were safely rescued and escorted to Gaurikund after a landslide blocked the route late Sunday night, officials said.The pilgrims were stranded around three kilometres from Gaurikund after a landslide hit the route near Chirbasa, news agency ANI reported.The Rudraprayag District Control Room (DCR) informed Sonprayag Police about the situation late on September 27, following which the SDRF Sonprayag team, led by Sub-Inspector Ashish Dimri, rushed to the spot.
Pilgrims carefully evacuated from landslide zonePrioritising the safety of the pilgrims, the rescue teams carefully assisted them across the affected stretch. Around 1,500 pilgrims were brought safely to the other side of the landslide zone and escorted towards Gaurikund.The operation was carried out despite continued rockfall and the risk of further landslides in the area. Rescue personnel coordinated the movement of pilgrims to ensure they crossed the dangerous stretch safely.Joint teams complete rescue operationThe coordinated efforts of the SDRF, NDRF and DDRF helped ensure that all the stranded pilgrims were safely evacuated from the affected area.Officials said the rescue operation was successfully completed despite the challenging conditions at the site.

US Pacific Commander Paparo discusses defense of Taiwan
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
05:12:47 UTC
14:12:47 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Admiral Samuel Paparo, commander of the US Pacific Command, will appear on the cover of Time magazine's Oct. 12 issue, with the magazine publishing an interview Thursday in which he discussed how a potential Chinese invasion of Taiwan could be deterred.
“I'm almost quoting Sun Tzu when I say winning without fighting is the acme of skill,” Paparo told Time, referring to the ancient Chinese military strategist and author of “The Art of War.” “Mission success for me is not to fight and win a war; it's to provide a deterrent capability so that we never go to war in the first place,” he said, per Time.
Paparo's command oversees approximately 400,000 military and civilian personnel across the Indo-Pacific region. The US Pacific Fleet consists of about 200 ships, including five carrier strike groups, and nearly 1,100 aircraft.
Paparo's primary mission is to deter aggression in the Indo-Pacific, with preventing a conflict over Taiwan a central concern. Time described his task as persuading Chinese leader Xi Jinping that the costs of using force against Taiwan would be prohibitively high.
“Twenty-five years ago the People's Liberation Army Navy was about 37 warships, and today it's 12 times that,” Paparo told Time. “Just in the last 18 months they've delivered two cruisers, eight destroyers, eight frigates, an aircraft carrier, 11 submarines, four amphibious ships, and four long-range combat logistics ships.”
He said he was particularly concerned about China's advances in space and missile capabilities and the rapid expansion of its nuclear arsenal. “They're moving toward world reach,” Paparo said.
Paparo described his current task as a delicate balancing act: ensuring China understands US military capabilities and the risks of conflict while protecting sensitive information that could let an adversary develop countermeasures.
He described the US approach as “deterrence by denial,” which seeks to convince an adversary that an attack cannot achieve its objectives. “We are not seeking the overthrow of the Communist Party,” Paparo said. “It's just that you should know that where America's direct vital interests are involved, there's a high probability of denying your aggression,” per Time.
Paparo has also proposed creating what he calls a “hellscape” in the Taiwan Strait if deterrence fails. The concept involves using large numbers of relatively inexpensive, mass-produced precision drones alongside conventional high-tech missile firepower to prevent or significantly delay a Chinese amphibious assault on Taiwan.
The strategy draws partly on lessons from Russia's war against Ukraine, where extensive use of drones has transformed the battlefield. Paparo first publicly described the hellscape concept in 2024, saying the US could deploy large numbers of uncrewed underwater, surface, and aerial systems around Taiwan to buy time for the US, Taiwan, and other partners to respond to an attack.
“We need not gain air or maritime superiority of a space; we need only deny its use to aggressors,” Paparo told Time.
Time noted that direct US military intervention in a Taiwan Strait conflict would not be automatic. Paparo's role is to build and maintain a military capability capable of countering China, while decisions about whether and how the US would intervene in a conflict would ultimately rest with the US president.
The Taiwan Relations Act provides the legal framework for US relations with Taiwan and calls for the United States to make available defense articles and services necessary for Taiwan to maintain sufficient self-defense capability. It does not require the United States to automatically defend Taiwan militarily in the event of an attack.
The potential costs of a conflict were highlighted by a 2023 war game conducted by the Center for Strategic and International Studies. In most of the scenarios examined, US, Taiwanese, and Japanese forces prevented China from successfully occupying Taiwan, but the losses were severe.
The CSIS study found that the US could lose two aircraft carriers and 10 to 20 large surface combatants in most scenarios, along with approximately 3,200 US military personnel. The US and allied forces would also lose dozens of ships, hundreds of aircraft, and thousands of personnel.
The war game was conducted before the recent war in Iran and therefore did not incorporate subsequent changes in US weapons inventories and munitions availability.
Paparo nevertheless expressed confidence in the US military's ability to prevail in a conflict. “I am confident in our ability to prevail,” he told Time. “What I am working toward is the margin by which we do, and that margin expresses itself in lives, capability, money, and time. I want to drive that bill down to zero.”

German security agencies face dilemma after victories for far right and far left
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
05:07:30 UTC
14:07:30 KST

German security agencies face dilemma after victories for far right and far left
BERLIN – September’s victories for far-right and far-left parties in German state elections have intensified official debate over whether security authorities can restrict secret information that might be passed on to Russia or criminal groups.
The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, which came close to winning an absolute majority in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sept 6, and the far-left Left Party, which came first in the capital Berlin on Sept 20, could both pose risks, senior figures in the ruling coalition say.
In Germany’s federal system, states have their own domestic intelligence agencies under local government control, which share information with each other and operate with the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV).
Politicians from rival parties and former security officials have expressed fears that if the agencies come under the authority of ministers from the far right or far left, confidential information could leak either to Moscow or, in the case of Berlin, to groups investigated over suspicions of organised crime links.
“This concerns information relating to organised crime – that would be an issue in Berlin,” said Alexander Hoffmann, head of the parliamentary group of the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democrats (CDU).
“And it’s about issues concerning Russia – that would be Saxony-Anhalt,” he said.
The AfD rejects accusations from rival parties that it is effectively allied to Russian President Vladimir Putin, saying that it seeks only to avoid war and opposes Germany providing military support for Ukraine.
An AfD spokesperson said the government was “clutching at straws in an attempt to discredit us in the eyes of the electorate”.
“It is telling that we have been confronted with such speculation and accusations for many years, yet the other side has failed to produce a single piece of evidence,” the spokesperson said in an emailed statement.
The Left Party did not immediately respond to a request for comment. But party leaders have previously said they considered as unacceptable any association with what German police identify as clan structures within the Kurdish, Lebanese and Palestinian communities in Berlin involved in organised crime.
The accusations of links to such groups are often intertwined with accusations of anti-Semitism, which the party also says it firmly rejects.
Source says security services are drawing up plans
The discussion over restricting confidential information has been underway ever since opinion polls pointed to a possible victory for the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt, where the local branch of the party is designated as right-wing extremist by the local office of the domestic intelligence agency.
Hendrik Wuest, the CDU state premier of North Rhine-Westphalia, earlier in September called for a special federal and state committee to be set up to consider how to deal with the issue of information-sharing with an AfD-led government.
“Of course, preparations are under way – but people are still waiting to see what happens, because it isn’t even clear whether the AfD and The Left will form governments at all,” said one security official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Despite coming first in the election in Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD fell short of the absolute majority it would need to govern alone, and its coalition options are restricted because the other main parties have all ruled out cooperating with it.
The Left Party is, however, likely to try to form a coalition with the centre-left Social Democrats and the environmental Greens, but both parties have demanded that it take action to eliminate anti-Semitism from its ranks.
Several of the AfD’s state party branches have been designated as far-right extremist groups by domestic security authorities, prompting the AfD in turn to accuse the intelligence services of political interference.
Officials are also concerned that security officials involved in investigating the AfD could be targeted by a future AfD-led administration.
Tensions between political parties and the security services have surfaced from time to time in recent decades, but the idea of systematic exclusion from information sharing underlines the gravity of the division.
Along with the main domestic security agency, the BfV, other security services and state governments are now considering restrictions, although security officials say they would not want to cut off all information-sharing, citing issues including indications of potential terrorist attacks.
Left Party representatives say terms such as “clan-related crime” often stigmatise entire ethnic communities and say that contacts with local residents do not imply support for criminal activity.
Like the AfD, it has long been suspicious of the BfV. The Left Party’s Berlin campaign programme called for the Berlin state agency to be abolished and replaced with “a transparent, democratically controlled body that is close to the people”.
However, one Left Party member of the federal Parliament has acknowledged social media contacts with a member of an extended family in Berlin accused of involvement with criminal groups and said he would “take the time to dispel any doubts” and “review my communication style”.
“There is absolutely no justification for elected representatives having contacts with individuals associated with organised crime,” Ferat Kocak said in a post on the social media platform X. REUTERS

Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns today
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
05:06:46 UTC
14:06:46 KST

Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.
Who is eligible for the gold ring?
The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.
These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas.
Scheme draws on Tamil tradition
Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.
Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.

Stories as a Resource: How Narrative Design Builds Resilience
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
05:00:00 UTC
14:00:00 KST

This article is part of "Thresholds", a special edition printed newspaper by Cobe Notes x ArchDaily.
There are two unique things about being human that made us survive the early years and spread over the whole planet: sweating and storytelling. Sweating helps cool down the body when running long distances. Stories help us collaborate in big numbers and share knowledge across groups and generations. As architects, we still rely on the same tools to make visions become reality.
As professor of stories Angus Fletcher points out in his book Primal Intelligence, there is a common misconception about the role of stories: when our "rational" brain has developed an idea that we fail to explain to a wider group, we pack it into a story, and suddenly everybody understands. Fletcher argues that it actually works the other way around: ideas come from stories, our brain works in stories, and stories form reality. Architects have a derogatory term for turning that process the wrong side up: "post-rationalisation", for example when diagrams are made to explain a design that is already decided.

US FDA approves Mirum’s drug for rare bone disorder
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
04:56:00 UTC
13:56:00 KST

US FDA approves Mirum’s drug for rare bone disorder
WASHINGTON - The US FDA on Sept 25 approved Mirum Pharmaceuticals’ pill for a rare bone disorder, offering patients a new treatment option that can help slow the disease’s progression.
The once-daily drug zilurgisertib, branded as Atebrioz, is approved for patients aged 12 years and older with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), which causes muscles, tendons and ligaments to gradually transform into bone, restricting movement and leading to severe disability.
Atebrioz blocks ALK2, a protein that is abnormally active in most patients with FOP and drives bone formation outside the skeleton. The recommended dose is 100 milligrams.
FOP is typically diagnosed in early childhood. About 300 people in the US and 900 worldwide, according to Mirum, have the condition.
Mirum expects to launch the drug in October and plans to announce its price at the launch, chief executive officer Chris Peetz told Reuters.
“It is a game changer for patients to have a medicine like this that can really stop that progressive, endless accumulation of bone,” Peetz said.
Citizens analyst Jonathan Wolleben estimates Atebrioz could cost about US$750,000 (S$958,410) annually and generate roughly US$150 million in peak worldwide sales.
Mirum had licensed the drug from Incyte earlier in 2026 for US$16 million upfront, along with potential milestone payments and sales royalties.
The approval by the US Food and Drug Administration was based on a 63-patient study, in which Atebrioz significantly cut new bone formation compared to placebo at week 24.
Current treatment options for FOP include Ipsen’s oral drug Sohonos and Regeneron’s Pasatru, a monthly infusion. Sohonos is approved for certain children and adults, while Pasatru is approved for adults.
Wolleben said Atebrioz could become a preferred treatment because it combines oral dosing with strong efficacy and a favorable safety profile, offering greater convenience than Regeneron’s monthly infusion and potentially fewer safety concerns than Ipsen’s Sohonos. REUTERS

BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Observers worldwide have said that a stable China-U.S. relationship serves not only the interests of the two countries but also those of the world, providing greater predictability for global trade.
Chinese President Xi Jinping's just-concluded U.S. state visit has led to new progress toward building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity.
In his talks with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday, Xi also called for translating the new vision of building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability into action and finding the right way for the two major countries to get along with each other.
"It aligns with the common aspirations of the international community yearning for stability, as stable Sino-U.S. relations will help anchor global peace and stability. It stands to disprove the inevitability of the Thucydides Trap myth in managing Sino-U.S. relations," said Ong Tee Keat, president of the Belt and Road Initiative Caucus for Asia Pacific.
As reality has time and again dawned upon the two major countries of the world that they have to accommodate each other in the current dynamics, peaceful co-existence is therefore the common denominator they need to cherish, said the Malaysian scholar.
Azmi Hassan, a senior fellow at Malaysian think-tank Nusantara Academy for Strategic Research, concurred, saying a good relationship between China and the United States will not only benefit these two major countries but the world.
"This is not only within trade but also in geopolitical terms, where both sides, and the whole world, can take advantage," he added.
"I believe it is critically important that the U.S. and China be on a trajectory in a positive direction as partners, and not on a trajectory of the adversaries," said Kenneth Quinn, president emeritus of the World Food Prize Foundation and a former U.S. ambassador to Cambodia.
Quinn, 84, who has led exchanges between the U.S. state of Iowa and China for decades, said his "number one goal" is that the China-U.S. relationship would continue its "constructive strategic stability" and "won't have that volatility, that up and down and huge increases in tariffs and planned tariffs."
"President Xi is absolutely right that stabilizing the China-U.S. relationship is critical. Creating a constructive relationship would be even better," said Bruce McLaughlin, CEO of Sinogie Consulting Group in Australia.
"Both sides benefit from a constructive, stable, well-regulated relationship that nurtures further trade and investment," McLaughlin said.
"What is vital here is that the U.S. administration stops seeing trade as a zero-sum game, and instead recognizes that it is possible to work toward mutual benefit," he added.
The leaders of the world's two largest economies meeting and talking directly is welcome news for business everywhere, said Rhys Roberts, national president of the Australia China Business Council. "What business values most is predictability."
"Commitments made at leaders' level matter most when they flow through into consistent, practical arrangements that companies can plan around. That is where business will be watching," he added. ■

13:32:14 KST

MACAO, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China's Macao Special Administrative Region saw a slight uptick in the unemployment rate for local residents during the June-August period, official statistics showed, as fresh graduates entered the labor market.
The local resident unemployment rate edged up 0.1 percentage point compared with the May-July period to 2.5 percent in June-August, while the local resident underemployment rate fell 0.2 percentage point to 2.0 percent, according to an official employment survey by Macao's Statistics and Census Service (DSEC).
Of the 7,500 unemployed local residents, most previously worked in gaming as well as wholesale and retail trade. New labor-market entrants hunting for their first job accounted for 18.9 percent of unemployed residents, up 6.7 percentage points, as recent graduates entered the workforce. Most of the 5,900 underemployed residents were engaged in business activities and construction.
Macao's general unemployment rate stood at 2.0 percent, a 0.1-percentage-point rise from the May-July period. The overall underemployment rate dropped 0.2 percentage point to 1.5 percent. ■

Column: Committed to China since 1979 -- on 20th anniversary of World Economic Forum's Beijing Office
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
12:32:12 CST
13:32:12 KST

by Klaus Schwab
The twentieth anniversary of the World Economic Forum's Beijing office is a deeply personal milestone for me. The office has been present in Beijing since 2006, but my own journey with China -- and the Forum's engagement with China -- began much earlier, in 1979.
In the autumn of 1978, I followed with great interest the first signs of China's reform and opening-up. Deng Xiaoping had emerged as the driving force behind a new course, based on modernization, pragmatism and greater engagement with the world. I was convinced that something of historic importance was beginning. I invited Deng Xiaoping to the 1979 Davos Symposium. He did not attend personally, but China sent a distinguished delegation of economists, led by Professor Qian Junrui of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. It was the first official Chinese participation in Davos.
A few months later, I travelled to China for the first time and subsequently led a delegation of 20 European chief executives. China was then very different from the country the world knows today. Its economy was still largely separated from global markets, its international business links were limited, and few outside China anticipated the magnitude of the transformation ahead.
I did.
My belief was not based on economic statistics. It came from what I encountered: the determination to modernize, the enormous human potential of the Chinese people, the importance attached to education and development, and a willingness to learn from the outside world while finding a distinct Chinese path.
Before China had become a global economic power, we decided to build a relationship for the long term. Over the following decades, the Forum became a bridge connecting Chinese leaders, entrepreneurs and scholars with counterparts from around the world. In 2006, we gave this relationship a permanent institutional home by opening our Beijing office. A year later, we launched the Annual Meeting of the New Champions -- the Summer Davos -- in China.
The transformation I have witnessed since my first visit is extraordinary. China has become the world's second-largest economy, a central part of global manufacturing and trade, and an increasingly important source of technological and scientific innovation. More than 800 million people have been lifted out of extreme poverty. Whatever challenges remain, the scale and speed of this development are among the defining developments of our era.
I remember especially President Xi Jinping's participation in Davos in January 2017, the first by a Chinese head of state. At a moment of growing doubts about globalization, he warned: "Pursuing protectionism is like locking oneself in a dark room ... that dark room will also block light and air." It was a striking message about the importance of openness and interdependence.
Today, China's international role is entering another phase. China is no longer only adapting to the institutions of the global system; it is increasingly seeking to contribute ideas and initiatives to the debate about how that system should evolve. In May, Foreign Minister Wang Yi announced that China would host the Xiong'an World Governance Forum this autumn. He linked the initiative to themes including sovereignty equality, international rule of law, multilateralism, a people-centered approach, and real actions.
One need not agree with every proposal advanced by any country to recognize the significance of this development. The great global challenges of the Intelligent Age -- artificial intelligence, climate change, economic fragmentation, security and technological transformation -- cannot be addressed by one nation or one political system. They require mechanisms of cooperation that are more inclusive, more responsive and capable of translating dialogue into action.
China will inevitably have an important voice in shaping that future, just as other major powers, emerging economies, international organizations, business and civil society must have theirs. A responsible global governance system cannot be built through confrontation or exclusion. It must be created through dialogue among different perspectives and interests.
Looking back over almost half a century, I am proud that the Forum recognized China's potential early, long before the scale of its rise had become conventional wisdom internationally. But I am even more convinced that the essential lesson of those years is about the future, not the past.
The bridges that matter most are the ones built before they become indispensable.
That was my conviction when I first travelled to China in 1979. It remains my conviction today.
Editor's note: The author is the founder and builder of the Geneva-based World Economic Forum, a non-governmental international organization dedicated to studying and discussing issues concerning the world economy and promoting international economic cooperation and exchanges.
The views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect those of Xinhua News Agency.

Denmark to roll out stun guns nationwide and allocate nearly 800 million DKK from 2027 to expand the police and PET
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
04:27:07 UTC
13:27:07 KST

Eight Danish municipalities did not meet the required staffing ratio in kindergartens in 2025, according to figures published Monday by Statistics Denmark.
The municipalities are Ringsted, Odder, Holstebro, Ikast-Brande, Struer, Brønderslev, Rebild and Thisted.
Under the political requirement, there must be at least one pedagogical staff member for every six children in kindergartens. In 2024, 14 municipalities failed to meet the requirement.
The trade union BUPL, which represents pedagogues working in Danish children’s institutions, noted that more municipalities now meet the requirement than before.
“Staffing ratios have improved, and that is an important first step to ensure the quality in our daycare institutions,” BUPL chairperson Elisa Rimpler said.
“But we are not at the finish line at all when it comes to giving children the quality they are entitled to.”
Since 2024, there has also been a requirement of at least one employee for every three children in nurseries.
Five municipalities failed to meet that requirement last year: Bornholm, Holstebro, Ikast-Brande, Thisted and Rebild.
Rimpler said the figures were not good enough and called on municipalities to increase their efforts.
“There is a need to build on top of this, because in many places the staffing ratios on paper are experienced as very far from reality,” she said.
“Both because managers, long-term sick employees, and pedagogues employed to support individual children are counted, and because many of the extra employees do not have the necessary professional qualifications.”
According to BUPL, the law does not require the employees counted in the staffing ratios to have professional training.
The union said the share of pedagogues among staff was 57% in 2019, compared with 50.6% last year.
Children, Elderly and Housing Minister Jacob Mark of the Socialist People’s Party, SF, said it was serious when municipalities failed to meet the legal requirement.
He said the minimum staffing ratios were working because more nurseries and kindergartens were getting more staff around children and nationwide cuts to staffing had stopped.
“But, as I also see, there are eight municipalities that do not meet the minimum staffing ratios. That is completely unacceptable. I am going to intervene against that,” the minister said.
Mark also criticized the practice of counting managers and long-term sick employees in the staffing figures. He said managers are not with children all the time, while long-term sick employees are not with them at all.
According to Mark, municipalities “just” need to hire more pedagogical staff.
The minister said he will send a letter to the eight municipalities that do not meet the requirements. The same municipalities will also face scrutiny from Ankestyrelsen, Denmark’s public authority for supervising municipalities and other public bodies.
Ankestyrelsen can impose a range of sanctions after assessing why a municipality is not complying with the law, including advisory opinions and fines.
“Now they have had four years. Now they must reach the finish line with those minimum staffing ratios,” Mark said.

====================================================================================================

Lung cancer deaths down 16% with low-dose CT screening: IARC
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
04:22:22 UTC
13:22:22 KST

Lung cancer deaths can be reduced through low-dose CT screening, which can also help detect the disease before it reaches advanced stages in people at high risk, according to an IARC assessment.
NEW DELHI: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people, while also reducing the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, an International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) working group has found.Published in The New England Journal of Medicine, the assessment found established evidence that low-dose CT reduces lung cancer mortality when used in people at high risk based mainly on age and smoking history.IARC convened a working group of 23 clinicians and scientists from 17 countries, including Dr Abhishek Shankar of All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, to assess the benefits and harms of lung cancer screening.The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history, typically at least 20 to 30 pack-years. Studies involving former smokers generally included those who had quit within the previous 10 to 15 years, with screening usually performed annually.In India, people aged 50 to 80 with at least 20 pack-years of smoking who are current smokers or quit within the past 15 years can contact the Indian Lung Screening Trial, led by Dr Abhishek Shankar at AIIMS, New Delhi, about screening.
Dr Shankar has invited eligible people to contact him for screening under the trial.The evidence behind the finding came mainly from randomised trials. In the US National Lung Screening Trial, people screened with low-dose CT had a 16% lower relative risk of dying from lung cancer than those screened with chest X-rays at seven years. The European NELSON trial also found lower lung cancer mortality among men screened with low-dose CT at 10 years.Based on this evidence, the IARC group classified low-dose CT as Group A, indicating established evidence that it reduces lung cancer mortality and the incidence of stage III or IV disease. Chest X-rays, with or without sputum examination, were classified as Group C, as their ability to reduce lung cancer mortality could not be established.However, the review cautioned that low-dose CT screening is not meant for everyone. False-positive results ranged from 1% to 42% across studies, depending on the screening protocol. Among those with false-positive results, 5% to 32% underwent at least one invasive procedure, with complications occurring in 10% to 22% of such procedures.
The review also estimated that 3% to 26% of lung cancers detected in randomised trials involving high-risk people could represent overdiagnosis, meaning cancers that might not have caused harm during the person's lifetime.The working group said effective lung cancer screening needs more than CT scanners, including systems for identifying eligible people, assessing risk, monitoring nodules, providing treatment and follow-up, along with smoking-cessation support. Organised programmes also require trained staff, quality assurance, adequate healthcare capacity and equitable access.
Anuja Jaiswal is a Senior Assistant Editor at The Times of India, with an impressive 18-year career in narrative journalism. She specializes in health and heritage reporting, expertly simplifying complex health information to make it engaging and understandable for readers. Her deep dives into heritage topics are well-researched, resulting in captivating narratives that resonate with her audience. Over the years, she has worked in Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh and West UP, gaining diverse on-ground experience that shapes her storytelling.

Taipei Confucius Temple holds annual Teachers’ Day ceremony
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
04:19:23 UTC
13:19:23 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taipei Confucius Temple on Monday held its annual ceremony honoring Confucius on the 2,576th anniversary of his birth, an event that coincides with Teachers’ Day in Taiwan.
The ceremony began at 6 a.m. at the plaza in front of Dacheng Hall and followed traditional rites honoring Confucius, who is revered as the Great Sage and Teacher. The annual ceremony consists of a series of traditional ritual procedures and is held each year on Sept. 28, Teachers’ Day in Taiwan, per a press release.
Taipei Deputy Mayor Lin Yi-hua (林奕華) served as chief officiant, while Kong Chui-chang (孔垂長), the 79th-generation direct descendant of Confucius, served as the temple's sacrificial official. City councilors, municipal advisers, outstanding teachers, and distinguished citizens also participated as ceremonial officials, joining the traditional rites to pay tribute to Confucius.
Students from Minglun Senior High School and Lishan Senior High School served as ceremonial attendants, while students from Chongqing Junior High School provided the ceremonial music.
Students from Dalong Elementary School performed the eight-row Yi dance, a traditional ritual dance accompanying Confucian ceremonies. Teachers and students from Kaiping Culinary School prepared the ceremonial food offerings.
Student participation from different schools has become an important part of the annual ceremony. Taipei Confucius Temple has previously highlighted the roles of students serving as ritual attendants, musicians, and dancers in preserving the ceremony's traditional forms.
Taiwan-Okinawa Confucian exchange
This year's ceremony also highlighted historical exchanges between Taipei Confucius Temple and the Kume Soseikai Association in Okinawa, Japan. A delegation from the association visited Taipei Confucius Temple and presented a certificate of appreciation, recalling exchanges that date back more than five decades, per the press release.
Historical research documents that representatives of the Kume Soseikai Association visited Taipei Confucius Temple in 1973 to study its Confucian ceremony and ritual practices as the group worked toward rebuilding the Confucius temple in Naha. Taiwan subsequently assisted, including Confucian tablets and ritual implements, during the reconstruction of the Kume Confucius Temple.
The historical exchanges continued through the 1970s and included Taiwanese participation in ceremonies in Okinawa. Academic research records that Taipei Confucius Temple and other Taiwanese organizations provided ritual objects and other assistance for the reconstruction of the Okinawa temple, which was completed in the mid-1970s.
More than five decades later, the renewed exchange at Taipei Confucius Temple highlighted the longstanding cultural links between Taiwan and Okinawa surrounding Confucian ritual traditions. The ceremony also featured the sounds of bells, drums, and traditional music, with teachers, students, and volunteers working together to conduct the rites.
Taipei Confucius Temple also prepared commemorative gift bags featuring an illustration of Confucius. The temple said the design was intended to convey the Confucian ideal of broadening one's horizons through learning and travel.
The annual ceremony is part of Taipei's effort to preserve traditional Confucian ritual and music culture while introducing those traditions to younger generations. The Taipei Confucius Temple has held Confucian ceremonies since the early 20th century, with the current temple complex's Dacheng Hall completed in 1929.

China lights up ‘super microscope’ hopes with world-leading electron gun beam

Advertisement
China lights up ‘super microscope’ hopes with world-leading electron gun beam
By observing matter at the atomic scale, the Hefei Advanced Light Facility could drive breakthroughs in microchips
2-MIN READ2-MIN
1
 Listen
Zhang Tongin Beijing
China has produced an electron beam using a cutting-edge electron gun, taking a step towards building a “super microscope” that could help drive breakthroughs in everything from Alzheimer’s research to advanced microchips.
The Hefei Advanced Light Facility (HALF) in central China’s Anhui province fired its first electron beam on September 20.
Bunches of electrons generated by the gun were accelerated by a 192-metre (630-foot) linear accelerator until they reached 2.2 billion electron volts, marking a milestone for the fourth-generation light source project.

“My wife and daughter are EU citizens. I am not. I’m always afraid something can go wrong”
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
04:00:00 UTC
13:00:00 KST

“My wife and daughter are EU citizens. I am not. I’m always afraid something can go wrong”

Amman Architecture City Guide: 11 Projects in a Capital Shaped by Migration and Stone
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
04:00:00 UTC
13:00:00 KST

Built across several hills, Amman has grown at a pace few Middle Eastern capitals have matched. The city has received successive waves of migration — Circassians in the late 19th century, Palestinian refugees in 1948 and 1967, the Iraqi population after 1990, and Syrians since 2011 — each reshaping its density and social profile. Locally quarried limestone, extracted from quarries across Jordan and required by law for façades since the 1970s, has become the city's only common visual denominator. Behind this material uniformity, however, lies a continuous dialogue between vernacular tradition and international ambition.
This condition has taken concrete architectural form over the past decades. The monumental scale of the Al-Iskan (Housing Bank Center), built in Shmeisani between 1980 and 1984, consolidated large-scale architecture as a symbol of the country's emerging financial capital. At the same time, prominent Jordanian architects, including Jafar Tukan and Ammar Khammash, developed a distinct architectural vocabulary that reinterprets stone masonry, topography, and the natural landscape in contemporary terms, producing museums, conservation centers, and environmentally responsive buildings of remarkable local sensitivity. More recently, international firms and technologies have expanded this urban infrastructure through new geometries and bioclimatic solutions.
